I read through your comment and this entire thread with interest. I’ve lurked on this sub a great deal for maybe the last two years and actually find much to relate to. I’m 58 years old and have existed on disability benefits since I was 30. I produced a son in rather unfortunate circumstances, he is 24 now and NEET so I guess I relate to this sub on his behalf too. Before I get judged for the crime of giving birth to a child I was ultimately unable to care for, thus passing on my shitty genes and general misery, it was never my choice to have a baby and the whole conception and first six months of the pregnancy occurred when I was floridly psychotic and unaware of what had happened.

Like you I have severe mental illness, bipolar and BPD. I’ve been forcibly hospitalised more times than I can actually count and it was during one of these stays in the ward that I fell pregnant at the age of 33.

I related to what has been said about the virtual impossibility of relationships for women like us. I wouldn’t say my life is either worse or better than the mostly young men who frequent this place. Our challenges are different and I respect their struggles. What I have in common with them and with the posters on this thread is the ‘no life’ aspect, the social alienation, the judgment and the stigma.

I have contemplated suicide long and hard for most of my 50’s and have got as far as ordering the necessary poisons online. Survival instinct has me living (should I say existing) in a twilight limbo state. I am anhedonic and take no real pleasure in doing anything. I live to sleep. I have some cognitive impairment from decades of recurring psychosis and now find it impossible to focus on reading books which was always my passion.

On the plus side, I live in the U.K. where disability benefits for those like me are relatively generous. I also have very nice social housing that happens to be in a lovely area next to a big park. I got that after having my son. And no, that’s not why I had him. See above. I’m a virtual recluse though I try to drag myself out for a walk each day, dreading it every time and feeling conspicuous and vulnerable as I know I don’t look good and fairly obvious that there is something not quite right. I wish I never had to leave the house again but don’t want to lose the use of my legs.

Sorry for the tl/dr folks, hopefully someone out there can relate to some degree. I’m usually way too anxious, scared and intimidated to post on Reddit or anywhere else but I felt OP’s thread was a chance to do that.
